A 62-year-old female visits her primary care doctor reporting persistent diarrhea lasting several weeks,
accompanied by facial flushing episodes. Her vital signs show: temperature 98.3°F (37.2°C), blood
pressure 114/75 mmHg, pulse 66/min, respirations 13/min, and oxygen saturation 97% on room air.
Pulmonary examination reveals wheezing. After receiving symptomatic treatment, she returns in two
weeks with continued diarrhea, dry skin with a non-specific rash, and noticeable cognitive decline.
What is the most probable underlying cause of her current symptoms? Answer Choices: (A) Increased
vasoactive intestinal peptide levels (B) Vitamin B12 deficiency (C) Pellagra due to malabsorption (D)
Niacin deficiency (E) Hypothyroidism leading to skin and memory changes (F) Carcinoid syndrome with
tryptophan depletion (G) Chronic liver disease causing vitamin deficiency (H) Small intestinal bacterial
overgrowth (SIBO) (I) Increased serotonin levels (J) Zinc deficiency due to chronic diarrhea
 A. Chronic liver disease causing vitamin deficiency
B. Hypothyroidism leading to skin and memory changes
C. Vitamin B12 deficiency
D. Increased serotonin levels
